# Third-party content

> **这页管什么**：别复制别人的内容——改写并给链接。
>
> 来源：<https://developers.google.com/style/other-sources> · CC BY 4.0 · 本文件是**规则摘要**，非原文全文。

## Core principle

Don't copy content from another source — it might violate copyright. Instead, **paraphrase and link**.

Applies to text, images, code, logos, and speech.

## Quoting and paraphrasing

Rather than quoting directly, paraphrase the idea and link to the original.

- Recommended: define the term in your own words, then link to the source.
- Not recommended: quoting a definition in block-quote style, even with a citation.

## Sources to avoid copying from

Unless you're certain of ownership:

- **Third-party sources** — documentation, websites, books, blogs, videos, images, podcasts.
- **Reference sources** — dictionaries, encyclopedias, Wikipedia.
- **Open source product documentation** — licensing ranges from "no reuse without attribution" to "complete freedom". It's not safe to assume you can reuse freely. When in doubt, don't.
- **GitHub content** — licensing varies by user; same caution.

## Attribution and linking

Link to outside material rather than reproducing it. Even with a citation, quoting source text directly is discouraged.
